statements.text: Repeal the law (HB 29, from 2024) that allows the decision of just three districts in the state to force a book title to be removed from all public school libraries statewide. The decision of a district to remove a title from school libraries should be a local decision limited to that district, as its board only represents the citizens of that district and should not be able to make decisions for those outside it.

statements.text: If repeal is not possible, amend the law to require at least two-thirds of the districts in the state to agree on a title’s removal for it to be banned from school libraries statewide—a high threshold requiring considerable statewide consensus rather than the current low threshold that can be heavily influenced by a small number of activists and a handful of school board members in localized pockets of the state.

statements.text: I am also proud to uplift the rights of our LGBTQ+ community as a Vice Chair of the Congressional LGBT Equality Caucus. I believe your gender, whom you love, where you live, or the color of your skin should not make it more difficult for you to be an American. Unfortunately, LGBTQ Americans continue to face discrimination in far too many facets of life. I will continue fighting for dignity, respect, and equality for all Americans.
statements.context: official website issue page 'Civil Rights and Equality'

statements.text: “Bullying is a serious issue that threatens our children’s safety and well-being,” said Congresswoman Sánchez. “When students see adults, including our country’s leaders, bullying marginalized communities, they think it’s acceptable. Sadly, we’re too often reminded of the devastating consequences of allowing it to spread. Our students deserve to learn in an environment where respect and kindness are the norm, not fear and intimidation.”
statements.context: introducing Safe Schools Improvement Act (bans bullying incl. on sexual orientation and gender identity)

statements.text: Our kids should be able to wake up and go to school every day without fear of being bullied when they get there. The Safe Schools Improvement Act will help deliver an educational environment that is free of harassment for every single one of our students. As a mother, I know this bill will bring peace of mind to parents, teachers, school administrators and staff, and I know it will make a difference for countless students in school hallways across the country.
statements.context: introducing Safe Schools Improvement Act with GLSEN and HRC

statements.text: No parent wants their child to be bullied at school. Schools must be a safe place for our children to learn and grow and be protected from bullying. The Safe Schools Improvement Act will give parents like me peace of mind to know all our children have an educational environment where they can learn without fear of harassment.
statements.context: introducing Safe Schools Improvement Act 2019

statements.text: Unfortunately, extreme MAGA politicians and state legislatures are actively trying to advance their hateful agenda. We must stand up for LGBTQ+ Americans—especially our trans and non-binary youth—in the face of these attacks. Together with my colleagues in the Equality Caucus, I will keep fighting to amplify LGBTQ+ voices and protect your right to love and be who you are.
statements.context: LGBTQ+ History Month statement

statements.text: I'm proud to join the LGBTQ+ community in celebrating the start of LGBTQ+ History Month. Throughout the month of October, we will honor the people, places, culture, and moments in history that make up the LGBTQ+ experience—an experience that is often left out of history books,
statements.context: LGBTQ+ History Month statement (sentence ends with comma before attribution in source)

statements.text: This year, as we celebrate Pride, we must also think about the extreme MAGA politicians and state legislatures actively trying to advance hateful and anti-equality legislation throughout the United States. I joined the Congressional Equality Caucus because I believe LGBTQI+ people deserve to live freely as their authentic selves and deserve full legal equality in the U.S. and around the world. I will continue to fight to protect LGBTQ+ Americans right to love and be who they are.
statements.context: Pride Month statement

statements.text: The Pride flag represents inclusion, diversity and equality. These are the values we should be uplifting as government leaders. Banning the flag from city hall sends the hateful message that these are no longer the values of our community. I strongly disagree.
statements.context: Downey City Council banned Pride flag at city hall

statements.text: As a vice chair of the Equality Caucus, I will continue to fly the Pride flag outside my congressional office. It’s important to me that all LGBTQI+ residents of Downey – and throughout my district – know they are seen, valued and loved.
statements.context: same statement

statements.text: Unfortunately, MAGA Republicans hijacked this year’s NDAA and attached extreme amendments that made the bill something I could not support. They turned a good and necessary piece of legislation into a bill that is anti-woman, anti-health, anti-diversity, and anti-LGBTQI+.
statements.context: explaining NO vote on FY24 NDAA

statements.text: Everyone, regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity, deserves to be protected and treated equally under the law. The Equality Act amends existing federal civil rights laws to ensure that LGBTQ Americans are afforded the same protections from discrimination that we all enjoy. I am proud to join a bipartisan majority of my colleagues to support this historic legislation.
statements.context: House passage of Equality Act

statements.text: It is unacceptable that the law today still treats LGBTQ people as second class citizens,
statements.context: Equality Act reintroduction (sentence ends with comma before attribution in source)

statements.text: Today, we have taken a historic step toward protecting marriage equality for LGBTQ+ and interracial couples,
statements.context: final passage of Respect for Marriage Act

statements.text: Transgender members of our military deserve national praise for their dedication and service to our country. They serve our country every day with distinction and courage. Instead, this morning they were demeaned by the commander-in-chief via Twitter. This has to stop.
statements.context: Trump announcement banning transgender military service

statements.text: For the past four years, the Biden administration has taken a sledgehammer to Title IX through rulemaking at the Department of Education (ED). This legislation would reverse the harmful ED rule that forces schools to allow males to share private spaces with females and compete in women’s sports—or risk losing their funding.
statements.context: office press release on cosponsoring Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (office text, not a direct quote)

statements.text: The Department must consider the resulting real-life inherent costs—the cost of lost opportunities for girls in academic settings. By expanding the pool of protected individuals and creating mass uncertainty at each individual school and school district, it stands to reason that biological girls will ultimately lose scholarship and athletic opportunities designated for them under the original intent of Title IX.
statements.context: signed joint public comment opposing ED Title IX athletics rule (fixed text, as quoted in his press release)

statements.text: Rather than expanding the definition of Title IX to fit the current progressive agenda, the administration should support Congress in strengthening its congressional intent and reinforce the protections Title IX afforded women and girls when it was first enacted in 1972.
statements.context: same signed comment

statements.text: This proposed rule reverts the playing field to a time before Title IX’s enactment and will cause irreparable harm to women entering academia and athletics,
statements.context: same signed comment, as quoted by Washington Examiner via Hyde-Smith site (sentence continues into attribution)

statements.text: National School Choice Week is a time to celebrate how families benefit from having the ability to choose the type of education that is best for their children. This choice has never been so important. With parents fighting to keep their kids in school throughout COVID-19 or to have a say in what they’re children are being taught, now is the time to empower parents’ control of their child’s education.
statements.context: parents' rights / school choice resolution; no gender reference in his words (resolution text cites CRT)
